clue.text: Impudence — the cane is somewhat meretriciously applied

parts.note: lip is cheek or impudence, as in 'none of your lip'
a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's cheek is punished with the cane, applied with a certain showy relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cane' looks like the punishment for impudence, but it simply gives STICK; the definition is a wry description of make-up laid on to attract.
explanation.definitionFit: Meretricious means flashily attractive, and this cosmetic is a colour worn on the mouth, often thought a touch showy.

clue.text: Brief study in a non-clerical context

indicators.note: in places the study word within the lay word

parts.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy
to con is to study or learn

explanation.surface: A short piece of study done in a secular setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses few words, so it is brief and terse.

clue.text: A literary pickle

parts.note: Tobias Smollett's novel is named after its hero, whose first name precedes the surname Pickle

explanation.surface: A tricky situation in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' suggests a predicament; it is Smollett's hero, Peregrine Pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of Smollett's hero Peregrine Pickle; a pickle in literature.

clue.text: The Psalmist would appoint no prince as one

definitions.text: The Psalmist would appoint no prince as one

parts.words: The Psalmist would appoint no prince as one
parts.note: Psalm 146 says 'Put not your trust in princes', so no prince is someone to be trusted

explanation.surface: King David would never put a prince in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Psalm text 'Put not your trust in princes' points to one trusted with property.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given legal control of property for others, a person placed in trust.

clue.text: In which the action should suit the' word

definitions.text: In which the action should suit the' word

parts.words: In which the action should suit the' word
parts.note: a parlour game where players mime a word, echoing Hamlet's 'suit the action to the word'

explanation.surface: Advice to an actor that gesture should match speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet tells the players to 'suit the action to the word'; in this party game the miming is meant to fit the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A party game in which players act out a word syllable by syllable for others to guess.

clue.text: A scarf may give rise to a quarrel

indicators.note: the letters of the first words are made to produce a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's scarf is the spark for a squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy brawl or disturbance is a quarrel in its loudest form.

clue.text: We get the gen in this arrangement

definitions.text: We get the gen in this arrangement

parts.words: We get the gen in this arrangement
parts.note: put 'in' before this word and it becomes a word for gen or facts

explanation.surface: An arrangement through which we are briefed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gen' is British slang for information; 'in this' means IN placed before the answer makes that word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordered arrangement, as of troops or aircraft in a set pattern.

clue.text: Mending a leg with bust support is taught at school

indicators.note: mending puts something broken back together, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a bra supports the bust

explanation.surface: Fixing a broken leg with a brace, as one learns in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mending' rearranges A LEG into ALGE, then BRA follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of mathematics using symbols for numbers, a standard school subject.

clue.text: A number perhaps deny pain with this

definitions.text: A number perhaps deny pain with this

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word could be arranged otherwise, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many people use this to shut out pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DENY into DYNE, after A and NO; the whole clue describes a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkilling medicine, something that soothes, which is how people deny pain.

clue.text: Rumour-spreader-not still at the drinks party ?

definitions.text: not still at the drinks party

explanation.surface: A gossip who never stands in one place at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: One who passes gossip round; also a guest who moves from group to group, mingling rather than standing put.

clue.text: Proceed to do a turn that's beneficial

parts.note: to proceed is to go

indicators.note: doing a turn means the word do is read backwards

explanation.surface: Going on stage to perform an act is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do a turn' sounds like a music-hall performance; here the 'turn' flips DO into OD after GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneficial does you good: a direct synonym.

clue.text: No good dreaming in this novel edifice ?

definitions.text: No good dreaming in this novel edifice ?

parts.words: No good dreaming in this novel edifice ?
parts.note: a bad dream plus a monastic building gives the title of a Thomas Love Peacock satirical novel

explanation.surface: A building where sleep brings only bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: Peacock's 1818 novel; 'novel' is both 'new' and the literary form, and 'No good dreaming' is a bad dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peacock novel whose title pairs a frightening dream with a religious house, the edifice of the clue.

clue.text: He's nice, perhaps in a celestial way

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is pleasant in a heavenly fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Celestial Empire was an old name for China, so 'celestial' is an old word for its people.
explanation.definitionFit: China was called the Celestial Empire, so celestial once meant of China.

clue.text: The matter of a golfer's understanding ?

explanation.surface: What a golfer grasps of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as under-standing: a golfer's standing position is the stance, and under is SUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter or material; and punningly 'under-stance', as a golfer's stance is how he stands.

clue.text: It points to heaven-hence the summons to the faithful

definitions.text: It points to heaven-hence the summons to the faithful

parts.words: It points to heaven-hence the summons to the faithful
parts.note: a slender mosque tower rises skyward and is where the call to prayer is made

explanation.surface: A spire pointing upward from which worshippers are called.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mosque tower, from whose balcony the muezzin calls Muslims to prayer.

clue.text: Memo take in one that's left over

indicators.note: the memo word takes in the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a memo is a reminder note
one is the article a

explanation.surface: A note asks you to accept a single leftover item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' sets A, for 'one', inside REMINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest has gone, the part left behind.

clue.text: On her entry little beasts become little angels

indicators.note: her entry means the word her goes into the other piece

parts.note: young animals such as bears or lions are cubs

explanation.surface: When she arrives, the little terrors turn into little angels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little beasts' reads as naughty children, but it means young animals, CUBS, which HER enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Winged infant figures in art are angels, and the word is used of sweet-looking children.

clue.text: Spaniard is one happy to rise in the house

indicators.note: in puts these pieces inside the house abbreviation

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in a down clue rising reads the word bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: happy means glad

explanation.surface: A Spanish man is glad to get up in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns GLAD into DALG; with I it goes inside HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish nobleman of the lower gentry, so a Spaniard of rank.

clue.text: But a not uncommon item on the menu

definitions.text: But a not uncommon item on the menu

parts.words: But a not uncommon item on the menu
parts.note: the dish of cheese on toast is split as a scarce piece, though it is commonly served

explanation.surface: Something frequently found on menus.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as rare bit, an uncommon item, yet the Welsh cheese-on-toast dish is common on menus.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a standard menu dish.

clue.text: What people receive that they have to return

definitions.text: What people receive that they have to return

parts.words: What people receive that they have to return
parts.note: earnings must be declared on a tax return, so what is received is 'returned'

explanation.surface: Things people are given and must hand back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' suggests giving back, but it is the tax return on which earnings are declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Money earned or received, which must be declared to the tax authorities each year.

clue.text: There's no getting away from it

definitions.text: There's no getting away from it

parts.words: There's no getting away from it
parts.note: an idiom for an undeniable truth read literally as a position with no exit

explanation.surface: Admitting an inescapable fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or dead end, a situation with no way out.

clue.text: A slow train

parts.note: a train is also a procession of followers, here a slow funeral one

explanation.surface: A railway service that crawls along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests the railway, but means a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral procession, a solemn file of mourners moving slowly.

clue.text: It got the Ancient Egyptians rattled

definitions.text: It got the Ancient Egyptians rattled

parts.words: It got the Ancient Egyptians rattled
parts.note: a metal rattle used in Egyptian worship, read as making them nervous

explanation.surface: Something that unnerved the pharaohs' people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattled' suggests unsettled, but this is a shaken rattle used in Egyptian rites.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal rattle shaken in the worship of Isis, an Egyptian percussion instrument.

clue.text: Lady climber, as sweet under any other name

definitions.text: Lady climber, as sweet under any other name

parts.words: Lady climber, as sweet under any other name
parts.note: a rambling rose named like a woman; Juliet says a rose by any other name would smell as sweet

explanation.surface: A woman mountaineer who would be just as pleasant if renamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' is a climbing plant, not a mountaineer; the Shakespeare echo from Romeo and Juliet points to a rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular pink rambling rose variety bearing a woman's name, so a 'lady' who climbs.

clue.text: Association formed by striker

explanation.surface: A society made up of people who hit things.
explanation.definitionFit: A society of members; also a heavy stick or bat used to hit with.

clue.text: He doesn't give away information, evidently

definitions.text: He doesn't give away information, evidently

parts.words: He doesn't give away information, evidently
parts.note: a seller of newspapers charges for the news rather than handing it out free

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped man who keeps secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't give away' suggests discretion, but means he sells the information, in newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of newspapers, who deals in the news for money.

clue.text: Sally tries new style — nothing in it

indicators.note: nothing in it means the zero goes inside the rearranged word
giving the word a new style means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Sally tries a fresh look with nothing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is the military word; 'new style' turns TRIES into SRTIE, and 'in it' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden attack out from a besieged position, a military synonym.

clue.text: Message travelling from pole to pole?

definitions.text: Message travelling from pole to pole?

parts.words: Message travelling from pole to pole?
parts.note: the wire carrying an old telegraph message is strung between telegraph poles

explanation.surface: A note sent across the globe from Arctic to Antarctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole to pole' suggests the North and South Poles, but means telegraph poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A wired message sent along cables slung between posts.
